en: She who, having played at dice, is the giver of supreme liberation through divine vehicles;

she whose nature is the reality of Śiva; she who takes the form of the syllable *Śrīṃ*; she who abides in the divine *liṅga*; she whose form is the syllable *Kṣauṃ*; she who is the source of vitality (*ojas*); she whose nature is the Word-Brahman (*śabdabrahman*); she who is Marīci, Viṣṇu, and Rudra.
O Mahākālī, resplendent with the jewel upon Your head, possessing the brilliance of the sun, the Fortune of Great Siddhi!
Victory, victory to You, O Kubjikā! You who cause the wheel of worldly activity to revolve; You who assume the form of the triple-path;
You whose nature consists of the powers of Will, Knowledge, and Action; You who possess manifold forms; Sovereign of infinite millions of cosmic eggs!
What is the *pādukā*? [The response: Three *añjali*s.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ Kṣmrīṁ Aiṁ Rmlvryūṁ, the Śrī-pādukā of the power of action (kriyā-śakti).
Aiṁ Rmlvryūṁ! O you whose forms are white and born of the *jam* syllable, accept this offering (*bali*)! Svāhā!
Invocation and so forth; mudrās; recitation; *hrīṃ svāhā*; hymn of praise.
O Goddess, you are the sovereign who bestows the perfection of sovereignty;
O Mistress who is the cause of all, you are the destroyer of all misfortunes.
Then follows the worship of the vessel: "Oṃ, salutation to the eternal lotus seat."
Aiṃ, obeisance to the lotus-seat. Threefold añjali.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Ymlvryūṃ, O Śrī, bestower of desires and wishes!
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Vmlvryūṁ, O you whose nature is the mire of the flesh, accept this offering! Svāhā! (2)
Invocation and so forth: the *yonimudrā*. Recitation: *Śrīṃ svāhā*. Hymn of praise.
And this *Tāmasīpākavākya* is the destroyer of all defects;
it is the most excellent fruit of the Goddess’s grace, bringing peace to all.
(**)(? || Samayāntakapūjā || Triangle || Homage to the Lotus Seat (Padmāsana) ||
The triple *añjali* (threefold salutation): Hrīṃ Klīṃ Kāmeśvarī, O Bestower of Will and Desire! Drāṃ Drīṃ Klīṃ Plūṃ Saḥ.
Aiṁ Hsauṁ Sauṁḥ! To the venerable sandals of Bhairava Vāgvādinī.
Hymn of Praise.
I bow to the venerable Śundarī, who is established eternally in the bliss of supreme joy,
radiant like the rising sun.
Then follows the worship of the jar (kumbhapūjā).
Salutation to the seat of all powers. [Threefold añjali.]
Hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ āṃ, the sandals for Amṛtā. The Amṛta-mudrā. 5.
Aiṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ, accept this offering for Sudhādevī, svāhā! Accept, accept, svāhā!
Recitation: Sāṃ Juṃ Saḥ Svāhā. Hymn:
I bow to the Supreme Power (Parāśakti), the giver of knowledge, who is the goddess of the gods, whose nature is like the moon, and who cuts asunder the noose of worldly existence with her axe.
Thus concludes the worship of the water-pot (kumbha).
Then follows the worship with lamps.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ: the venerable sandals consisting of divine knowledge.
Hsrauṃ Hsklhrīṃ Hsauṃḥ Hskhphrauṃ Rā Kuleśvarī Kāmāgnaye Svāhā.
The worship of Trikūṭana; the invocation and so forth; the worship of Laya; the worship with the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of Ali.
Bali: Aiṃ Rāṃ! To Agni, known as Dīpatejas, and to Bhaṭṭārikā, Ḍaṃ Klinne Svāhā! Accept this bali! (2) Hūṃ Phaṭ! Japa: Hsklhrīṃ Svāhā! Stotra: [Hymn of Praise]
You alone are the creation, sustenance, and destruction of all embodied beings;
you are the pervasive radiance of the entire universe—O Śrīsundarī, salutations, salutations!
Dīpajapet || Mantra ||
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ Kclhrīṃ Hsklhrīṃ Nklhrīṃ Śrī-Kāmāgnaye Svāhā Sklhrīṃ Hsklhrīṃ Kclhrīṃ Sauḥ Hlīṃ Aiṃ. This is the mantra. Dhāra (27).

O Goddess, you who are the sprout of bliss for the Kṣatriyas of the Supreme Brahman, such as the Sun, Moon, and Fire whose rays are like grains of pollen; you who possess a body of three coils extending from Śiva to Āditya,
you who swallow the universe— wondrously, O Blessed One, you manifest within the heart of your devotee!
Then follows the offering of the bali.
Śrīṁ Hrīṁ, salutation to the King of Mantras. Oṃ Hsrauṁḥ Sthūla Hrīṁ Śrauṁ, salutation to Ādi Tripurā.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Hsauṃḥ, obeisance to Tripurabhairava. (2) Aiṃ Hrīṃ Saḥ, obeisance to Vāk Tripurā.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sauṃ Mahālakṣmī (2). Aiṃ Hrīṃ Sauḥ Vahni Tripurāyai (2).
Aiṃ Glauṃ Klīṃ, [salutation] to Mādinī. (2)
Oṃ aiṃ klīṃ blūṃ ya, to Tripurā, who is Bhrāmarī. (2)
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Bhrāṃ Phreṃ Hasau, [salutation] to Trailokyasvāminī. (2)
Aiṁ ḍāṁ ḍīṁ ḍūṁ, to Ḍākinī (2). Oṃ sauḥ, to Kālikā Tripurā (2).
Aiṃ Aiṃ Sauṃḥ, to Cāmuṇḍā (2). Aiṃ (2) Sauṃ, to Tālamadhyamā (2).
Aiṃ (2). To Kapālāṭkulavāsinī Tripurā (2). One should worship the lamp with the mantra of the four seats.

Then, having performed the daily worship of Cakreśvarī, Vaṭuka, and the others, including Indra and the rest, with the mantra *Oṃ Khaṃḍāva Śrībhairavī Hsaṃ*, one should perform the worship of the deities of the directions and so forth as prescribed in the Āgamas.
Those five powers [are applied] with the root mantra for the kindling of the lamp-flame.

Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁ! O you adorned with ornaments of human entrails, O Mahākaulinī, O speaker of the Great Brahman, O you who intoxicate with great wealth, O bestower of all enjoyments, make this body of mine composed of adamant; slay the wicked twice; drink the earth and blood twice; shatter the wheel of flesh twice.
Victory to Kālī, who traverses the sky, the sovereign of the three worlds!
YMLVRYŪṂ RMLVRYŪṂ KṢMLVRYŪṂ! O Śrī Bhairavī, by your grace, svāhā!
Then, in the section on the recitation of the ritual manual, one should perform the rite of auspiciousness (*svastikuryāt*) and so forth.
O Kuṇḍalinī, born from the ear-rings, illuminator of the lamp of power,
divine, bestower of knowledge, peaceful, granter of desires, supreme giver of liberation.
Accompanied by honey and curd, this lamp of fire within the realm of desire destroys all the darkness of suffering from the world;
it burns away every sin and purifies the seat of purification.
The family lamp of the three worlds, whose form is fire, moon, and sun.

This [work], overflowing with prose, dispels the darkness [of ignorance], illuminates the light of knowledge, and is filled with inner splendor; it is composed of refined gold, joined with camphor and saffron,
awakening consciousness, bestowing all auspiciousness, and removing the suffering of poverty.
May this lamp, fashioned by celestial maidens, be pleasing to the illustrious Sundarī.
One should perform the salutation to the lamp. [This is done with] the Trikhaṇḍā mudrā and the Lelihā mudrā.
Aiṁ Klīṁ Sauṁḥ Kclhrīṁ Hlkhrīṁ Sklhrīṁ Klīṁ Plūṁ Nityakāmeśvarī Strīṁ Sarvaśaṅkari Saḥ Tripurabhairavī Aiṁ Vicce Klīṁ Tripurasundarī Devī Śrīpādukām.
The sevenfold stream of the Tripura-gāyatrī (7). The offering of the bali-oblation with the aim of fulfilling desires.
Recitation: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Svāhā.
Hymn of Praise.
You are the form of creation, maintenance, and dissolution; you are the beloved of all the gods in this world where you sustain the earth with your excellent power.
You are the perfection (*siddhi*) granted by the gods, and all the hosts of asuras and sages are your practitioners (*sādhakas*) in due order.
You are the one who follows after all actions, consisting of all virtues, and you strike down the violent impulses of the universe.
I bow to that essence, which is the form of light that destroys the fire of the darkness of the cause of saṃsāra.
The mudrās for invocation and so forth; the Jvālinī mudrā.
Then one should prostrate; one should recite the *bhramaṇa*.
O Bliss, O Bliss, you who shine with unfailing splendor, O Svacchandā, *klīṃ*!
I take refuge at the feet of Śrīsundarī, the digit of Śiva, the compassionate goddess whose heart is the heart of Hara, and whose radiance is intensely and incessantly flashing forth.
Āṃ īṃ, O Ānandavallī, you who bestow the nectar of immortality; Drāṃ drīṃ, you who are the supreme Śakti; Māyī, whose form is the syllable of Māyā;
Sphaṭikenaṇimayī, whose body is like crystal; Māmatāṅgī, the wielder of the sword.

O Knower, whose form is the essence of knowledge, who is composed of the *narina* sound, whose mantra is the *hūṃkāra*, who is seated in the *yogāsana* with the syllables *klīṃ* and *pluṃ*, O beautiful one, who is the moon of the world, *aiṃ*: salutations to you!
The young mantra-practitioner, Kaṇakṣī, is blissful in my heart, fierce in the realization of the mantra;
she wears a serpent as her sacred thread, stands upon the broad slopes [of the mountain], and shines with heroic power.
Hrīṁ Aiṁ! She whose crown is the crescent moon, who is seated upon a bull and a serpent, is independent.
O you who take the form of the *kālikā* plant, whose nature consists of the qualities of *ka*, *kha*, and *ga*, O compassionate one, *klīṃ*, homage to you!

She who dwells at the root, the Great-Souled One, who is the fire of digestion, who is the embodiment of all mantras, the three-eyed one, she who wears captivating armlets and garlands, she who stands upon the three worlds, the Mother, the Sky-farer;
she who is the altar, the voice of the Vedas, the giver of intense bliss, the Heroic Essence— she is Bhavānī.
O essence of the essence of saṃsāra, you who are difficult for all to traverse, O Sovereign of All Splendor, *sauḥ*, homage to you!
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ! O Sāradākhī, bestower of the tradition of all perfections;
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Drāṃ! O foremost of seed-syllables, giver of the form of light illuminated by beneficial rays;
Bhlūṃ Glauṃ Kṣauṃḥ! O power of mantra, immeasurable as the Praṇava, the Bindu, and the end of Nāda.
KṢĀṂ KṢĪṂ KṢŪṂ! O destroyer of desires, you who have swallowed the Kali age like a morsel of food, salutations to you!
Āṃ Krauṃ Klīṃ! You whose form is meditation, who removes the fear of the trident, who dries up the minds of the distressed;
you who wear the seat of Prakṣaṣī upon your crown, who hold the clouds of universal dissolution, who possess the three forms of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva;
you whose self is pure, whose form is pure, who agitate the hosts of gods and sages, O power of the unshakeable!
I bow to her whose form consists of creation, maintenance, and dissolution, who is composed of the destroyer of Tripura, and who possesses a formidable appearance.
The lamp-eating, the manifestation of desire.

Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Oṃ Hrīṃ! The splendor of the Self, the external splendor, the lamp of the Kula born of the *kuru* [seed-syllable], the supreme light of the *mūlādhāra*, that "I am" (*so'haṃ*)—the venerable Point of Light (*jyotirbindu*).
The bowl.

This Navātman, the nectar of the three sections, is served by the illustrious Śaṅkara; it enters the lunar nectar; it is protected by the sovereign of Kṣatras; it is honored by the hosts of Yoginīs and the great Siddhas; and it bestows the arrival of bliss. Sākhya! [Recite] this.
I bow first to that vessel resting upon a lotus, which bestows the threefold purity.
Oṃ amṛte amṛte amṛtodbhave svāhā. Having made [it] a space-dweller (*khecarī*), one should consume it with its respective mantra.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! You are the very nature of the bodily constituents—skin, flesh, fat, and bone.
Therefore, I consume you today; I offer the supreme sense-organ as an oblation, Hūṃ Svāhā!
Furthermore, O Pātra: [he who is] endowed with a multitude of arts that harmonize with all traditions, and who possesses a sense of wonder.

Salutations to the second vessel, served by Indra, Upendra, Mahendra, hosts of Kinnaras, Brahmā, and others; from which the purity issuing from the deities of meditative concentration always arises at the mouth for the increase of the happiness of the worlds—this has been composed. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ Svāhā.
The consumption of aquatic creatures.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! I offer into the fivefold fire that which has arisen in the form of Time (Kāla), having the appearance of fish-skin; Oṃ Svāhā, I sacrifice this.
The vessel; the consumption of the earth-dweller.
I offer into the fire of the vital breath all that is fierce, possessing the form of a jackal in the wilderness, and joined with the piercing [of] each respective reality.
The vessel: Oṃ, I offer the reality in the left; svāhā!
The consumption of the crest-ornament.
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ! I offer into the fire of the Self the crest-ornament and ginger, resplendent with the essence-element. Oṃ Juṃ Saḥ, to the crest-ornament, Svāhā!

The Vessel: One should mutter the *mṛtyuñjaya* mantra, which is the abode of the glorious and auspicious vessel, as prescribed by Kāma; it brings about the subjugation of dense sovereignty. Then, one should perform the *saṃvartana* oblation (*caru*) and subsequently the worship. This is the worship of all the *carus*.
Having drawn a triangle, a hexagon, a circle, and a square, [perform] the four purificatory rites and the *dhenumudrā*.

One should recite [the mantra] seven times over the deceased. Having performed the rite, one should offer it to the Yoginīs. This is the consumption of the sacrificial pap (*caru*) for all. Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ! O Giver of Food, Giver of Life, may life arise through this food! Kākālī, Mahākālī, Consumer of the Sacrificial Pap, Svāhā!
The bowl.
Salutations to you who have come before me in a beautiful form, O Goddess of gods;
your touch, sight, knowledge, and consumption bestow liberation.
The consumption of egg-born creatures.
Aiṁ, pierce! (2) O you who perform all actions, svāhā! [This is] the consumption of half-cooked food. Oṃ klīṁ sauṁḥ svāhā!

The pair of qualities describing reality after reality has reached the stainless Fish [incarnation], which bestows immortality upon all that is moving and unmoving; may that supreme one, consisting of knowledge and the knowable,
who is bliss and sovereignty, the vessel for the worlds, and the purifier of the copper-like world, be victorious.
It is the supreme subjugation for yogins; it is the consumption of [the sacrificial] remains.
Aiṃ drāṃ klīṃ plūṃ strīṃ saḥ svāhā.
I am one who has painted the city with wine, I am the descent of the worship of Yoga, I am one whose self is cultivated through many kinds of ritual practices,
I am one who has turned away from the state of the ignorant, and I am one who has taken refuge in Bhairavī.
I am the one who has taken refuge at the feet of the Guru; I am Bhairava; I am Śiva.
One should cause it to be circumambulated three times to the right.
Jayantikā for the journey. No seal. Praise of Forbearance.
O Great Goddess, my vision is clouded by the darkness of ignorance; I do not know [you].
O Sovereign, may you forgive me out of compassion; may you forgive me, may you forgive me, O Śivā!
O Mistress of Flesh, forgive me, your wretched servant, for this [offering] which is deficient in ritual, deficient in mantra, and deficient in substance, O Mistress of Flesh!
I do not know how to invoke you, nor how to worship you, nor how to dismiss you;
I do not even know the ritual procedure. You alone, O Supreme Goddess, are my refuge.
In deed, thought, and speech, may my conduct always be righteous;
for you, O Sovereign of the Universe, are the inner witness of all beings.
O God, the god is both the giver and the enjoyer; indeed, this entire world is the god.
The deity recites everywhere; that deity is Maheśvara.
The libation.
"Pratipretā," and so forth; the dismissal of the bali offering; the salutation to the heroes (vīra).
When the circle of heroes (vīracakra) has been joined, all castes are considered twice-born (dvija);
when it has reached the end of the circle, they are all again remembered as being of separate castes.
The food offering; the worship of the lunar disc; the betel leaf offering; the consecration with the ritual water-pot.

The stream of [blessings] has descended. O heroic ones, having joined your palms together with mutual flowers and consecrated rice, may there always be the complete destruction of obstacles, prosperity, auspiciousness, and well-being.
Salutations to you in your form as Bhairava; salutations to you, O Sovereign Lady of the World.
All the gods and goddesses, together with their retinues, assembled;
the Goddess was served with foods prepared according to the prescribed methods.

Whatever deficiency or excess may arise in this worship, O Lord, may the goddess Bhairavī, who is complete in all respects, graciously remedy it for me. Go, go to the supreme abode; return to your own respective dwellings.
But at the time of worship and propitiation, may you become victorious once again.
Having performed obeisance to the deity and the guru, [the mantra] shines as if dissolved into one's own self within the wheel.
One should move to one's own respective place.
[Thus ends the ritual procedure for the awakening of the lamp according to the doctrine of the Upper Tradition within the illustrious Kula teaching.]
May there be delight for the deity Śrīpāla.
May there be auspiciousness.
(1) In the Gaṅgā, Puṣkara, Narmadā, Sarayū, Yamunā, Godāvarī, Gomatī;
at the sacred sites of Gayā, Prayāga, Govardhana, Vārāṇasī, and the Indus.

Throughout the duration of the aeons, within the vessel of the universe beginning with Sarasvatī and the rest, the water of the Śrīcakra bestows the fruit of ten million billion ablutions in sacred fords. May it be auspicious!
(1) In the year 720, on the fifth day of the bright fortnight of Phālguna, the writing was completed.
May there be auspiciousness at all times!

(1) What suffering whatsoever is not destroyed when the Mother of all beings is remembered? O you who are as dark as the family of crows' infamy! What excellence is not attained when she is worshipped? What divine delight does she not bestow when she is praised? What protection is not obtained when she is protected? And what yoga does she not gather for the one who meditates upon her in the funeral pyre?
The two venerable sandals (*śrīpādukā*) reside within the "I-consciousness" (*ahaṃśeṣa*) of the supreme Śiva, who is eternally of one flavor (*samarasa*) with the Goddess Viśimānandā. || 1 ||
O Lord, one should worship the eternal Śakti, the mother of all limbs [of the universe], who possesses all powers and performs the fivefold cosmic acts. || 2 ||
Protected by Indra and the other guardians, and resplendent with supreme sovereignty, I worship the western gate, which is considered the abode of Mṛḍānī. || 3 ||
I bow to the elephant-faced Lord of the Gaṇas, whose hands hold a noose, a goad, and a fruit, who is radiant, pot-bellied, and the destroyer of obstacles for heroes.
Holding the radiance of her forehead between the two ends of her bow,

she who possesses the splendor of *sauṃ* and *klīṃ*, who is cool yet fair, the subduer, the immortal one who protects from all sides— this very Tripurā, ever abiding like the sun in the sky of the heart, may she swiftly sever your bonds.
She is the destroyer of Tripura, consisting of light and consisting of speech.

Aiṃ (5) Svāhā! O Mārtaṇḍa, speak! May the Dakṣiṇā and the Goddesses be auspicious; may the gods be auspicious! [May] the earrings [be] for you, O [Lord] whose splendor is supreme, who illuminates the joy of the world, whose brilliance is supreme, and whose wisdom is [the highest]. May the offerings be satisfied, and may there be well-being!
The ancestral fire-gods and all deities have been saluted; O you whose form is light, homage be to you!
O Island, worship this triad, which is blazing and the destroyer of evil.
They burn away all evils, removing those committed throughout seven lifetimes.
All that has been done everywhere removes the darkness of ignorance.
The Illumination of All Lamps is the purification of the sacred body;
it has emerged from the Moon-Lamp and completely pervades everything.
May the peaceful ones grant well-being and constant prosperity;
may they bring about auspiciousness and, by the mere sight of them, become a source of joy for all.
She burns away sins, she is the destroyer of impurities;
the Goddess brings peace to all and is the ender of obstacles and the liberator from curses.
The Yoginī who has severed her seat with a lamp bestows both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Now follows the worship with lamps.

Victory, victory to Baṭukanātha, the bestower of success upon practitioners! With his hand holding a skull-cup, his ears adorned with earrings, staff in hand, and bowing to Meru (?), he is the manifestation of primordial wisdom, the ritual observance of the Krama tradition, the destroyer of obstacles, and the sun;
may he triumph through this fourfold [prayer].
O Vātuka, who grants all accomplishments and brings peace, may you, who are worshipped by bhūtas and vetālas, be ever satisfied with my offerings and grant me constant tranquility.
May he who is like one desiring to protect, who is accompanied by the host of Kṣatrapāras, and who is ever delighted— may this Kṣatrapāra perform constant worship and grant me all protection.
O King of Obstacles, who at all times consumes all actions, destroy [them] for me; grant me peace and may you always protect me, O Lord of the Gaṇas.
(1) Aiṃ Hrīṃ Khphreṃ RyvLvkṣmryūṃ, obeisance to Pūrṇeśvara and Pūrṇeśvarī.
The former.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Khhphreṃ RylvKṣmryūṃ, salutation to Niśānātha (the Lord of Night) and Diśeśvarī (the Sovereign of the Directions). [South]
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hykṣmlvryūṃ! To Kujanātha and Kujeśvarī, Pāpū!
By the western [gate].
Oṃ pheṃ siddhikalāli hrīṃ cchrīṃ hūṃ strīṃ namaḥ svāhā || 16 || [The Uttarā]
Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauṃḥ Kaṃ 6 Haṃ Va Saṃ 5 Śrītripurasundaryai Namaḥ. (Above).
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Khphreṁ Hrīṁ Aiṁ Sauṁ, obeisance to Hāṭakeśvarī. [This is] for the half-offering. These [mantras] belong to the six Āmnāyas.
Then, having risen at dawn and completed the daily rites of purification, bathing, the twilight prayers, libations, and other obligatory duties;

Having gone to the sacrificial pavilion (yāgamaṇḍapa), performed the offering of the oblation (bali), and sat upon his own seat, he should begin from the beginning to the end the worship— including the primary and secondary limbs— of Vākya-dīpa-yāga Udyāna Sūrya, including the offering of arghya.

Perform the recitation (*japa*), the libation (*tarpaṇa*), and the dismissal of the offerings (*balivisarga*). Then, [perform] the *sagvaṇa*, the *mohani*, and the application of sandalwood paste and other [unguents].
The sacrificial fee for the gods.
"Just as there is no escape from the strikes of arrows," and so forth; elsewhere, there is no refuge.
The worship of Śakti purifies something.
One should cause the eight-limbed prostration to be performed and dismiss the Goddess and the others to their respective places.
Having worshipped Hṛtikā upon the pervasive maṇḍala and having placed the sacrificial offering (bali),
one should worship Caṇḍeśvara and Uciṣṭabhairava.
Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, to the assembly of pretas (2). Having offered the *caṇḍanādi* [fragrant substances], Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, Caṇḍeśvara Ucchiṣṭabhairava, accept the *bali* (2) Huṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
May the entire Brahmāṇḍa, including the śekhas, piṭhas, upapiṭhas, and so forth, be satisfied; svāhā!
Praise.
One should behold the three-eyed Bhairava, who has the luster of Krishna, holding a mace, a trident, a drum, and a drinking vessel, and who is the dispeller of all obstacles.
Displaying the *tarjanī-yonimudrā*, one should offer the *bali* oblation. The *balipūjā* is performed according to the prescribed method.
Then follows the worship of Kumārī.
Aiṃ, to the lotus seat (2). Aiṃ, to the peacock seat (2).
Meditative absorption.
Mounted upon a great peacock, Kaumāri possesses a most beautiful form;
she is clothed in red garments and subsists on blood and flesh.
O Goddess, you who delight in red flowers, whose body is as crimson as vermilion,
having one face and red eyes, and adorned with a hanging garland of severed heads.
The Goddess Śaktisūtrakalā, who wears a skull and the *bindu*,
dwells in the great sacred field of Kolāpuri under a banyan tree.
O you who eternally abide on the southern seat as Kaumāri, salutations to you!
Three *añjali* gestures (3).
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrī Caṃ (5) Ko Kmlvryīṁ U Ū, to the goddess Kaumārikā, together with Caṇḍabhairava, [I offer] the sandals.
Aiṃ! Let us know the Kulakumārikā; let us meditate upon the mantra of ten million syllables; may she impel that for us, Krauḷī.

The heart-mantra and other limb-mantras; the offering (*bali*) with the root mantra; the six *ḍākinīs*; the eight Mothers beginning with Brahmāṇī (8); the eight *Bhairavas* beginning with Aśitāṅga (8); the world-protectors (*lokapālas*) beginning with Indra (10)—these are the offerings for worship.
Again, O root-person: perfume, flowers, incense, lamps, food offerings, libations, three *añjali* gestures, and the sacrificial offering (*bali*).

Displaying the *yoni-triśikhā-mudrā*, perform the recitation (*japa*) and the hymn of praise (*stuti*). [Offer] the libation (*tarpaṇa*) to Haṃsī, who resides in the eastern direction and has the luster of a mass of vermilion. Offer the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the dismissal (*visarjana*), and the shadow of worship (*pūjā-chāyā*). [Perform] the general vessel (*sāmānya-pātra*) and the offering of the *bali* to the Brahmins. Thus ends the *Komāli*.
Then, [perform] the moon-sacrifice (candayāga) before the Goddess.

According to the sequence of the instruction, one should perform the worship of the feet of Śambhu—the white, red, mixed, and nirvāṇa [aspects]—according to the words of the Guru; [then follow] the Guru-vessel and the libation.
Having performed the satiation with sandalwood and other substances, one should worship the sandals of the venerable Guru.
Bali. Displaying the *kṣecarī-cinmudrā*, perform 108 recitations (*japa*). [Recite] the hymn (*stotra*).
Śrīnātha and the others; blinded by the darkness of ignorance; the friction of manifold powers; bliss, supreme bliss.
Salutations to you, O Lord, Blessed One, Śiva, who appears in the form of the Guru.
O you who have fully accomplished the descent of knowledge and have assumed various forms!

Salutations to Siddhinātha, whose nature is the Supreme Self, who possesses a form like that of the new moon, and who is the master of accomplishment for the purpose of shattering the darkness of all ignorance.
Salutations to the Self of Śiva, who is independent, whose form is fashioned by compassion,
who is dependent upon the devotion of his devotees, and who takes the form of worldly existence for those lacking devotion.
To the one who grants discernment to the discerning, deliberation to the reflective,
illumination to those who shine, and who is the very embodiment of knowledge for the wise.
One should pay homage in front, on the sides, behind, above, and below; O Creator, may you remain well-disposed toward me, both externally and in the form of my vital breaths.
[Thus ends the Hymn to the Guru in the King of Tantras.]
I always bow to the Guru with the eight-limbed prostration; [this is] the libation.
Having worshipped the Śaktis in due order, having offered the vessel of the Śakti, and having worshipped the entire host of Vīras,
one should take the remains of the Śakti offering and, being pleased, complete that [offering] for the Pretas and others.
One should give sacrificial fees (dakṣiṇā) to the feet of the Guru, to the Yoginīs, and to all the Vīra persons.

Homage! The Offering to Brahman: Oṃ. Whatever has been done by me from this moment until the departure of life—whether in the states of waking, dreaming, or deep sleep—through body, mind, speech, hands, feet, belly, or generative organ; whatever has been spoken or remembered—all that is an offering to Brahman. Svāhā!
May I and my own hand be offered to the venerable Guru; [this is] the mantra, svāhā!
One should drink that which is dissolved into one's own self. Having set aside the Guru-vessel, the Śrī-pātra is set aside.
Having recited the Jayatikā, one should turn the bowl face down.
Then, having established the patron in the svastika posture, one should cause him to undergo the consecration.
With the water from the ritual jar.
Oṃ Gaṅgā, Sindhu, Sarasvatī, Yamunā, Godāvarī, and the oceans— having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) with these mantras at every moment, one is always purified of all impurity.
At its conclusion, for one who desires long life, there is the seat of compassion (karuṇāsana) along with all its parts.
May she who is the cause of all prosperity and the conqueror of death protect you.
Candana, Sindūra, Sagvana, Mohanī, Svāna, Ārati, and finally Tejo.
The establishment of the words of auspiciousness; seen in the mirror; for the delight of the power of the jar.
Having taken up the three vessels of caru, one should consume the remaining caru from those three circumambulations for the purpose of drinking and eating.
As before, they perish; who would recite that even today when there is no food for heroes?
The worship of Kalaṅka; taking betel-leaf and returning to one's respective place.
[Thus ends the ritual procedure for the commencement of each [practice], illuminated by the very brief *Caru* of the family commitment (*kulasamaya*).]
(1) The vigil of the sacrificial animal.
A black-colored bull that is difficult to subdue, young in age, with glossy flesh and a body as if imbued with nectar— for such a bull, the offering of the *bali* is highly praised.
In the cup: Hrīṃ Kāli Vajeśvari, homage to the iron-staffed, sharp-edged sword! (2)
Hrīṃ Vāgeśvarī (2). Hrīṃ Umāmaheśvarāya (2).
Hrāṃ, to Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva, joined with Śakti, [and] Khaḍga. (2)
"To Khaḍga, to the destroyer of evil," and so forth.
Having performed the *calasa-pūjā* with the *astramantra*,
one should offer the *piṃkhālaṃcha* with the *maitra-mantra*.
All animals exist for the sake of sacrifice, and the slaughter of animals is for the sake of sacrifice;
therefore, I shall kill you, for in a sacrifice, killing is not truly killing.

Having performed the *nyāsa* with the weapon-mantra (*astra*), offered the water of honor (*arghyajala*), and consecrated [the offering] as nectar (*amṛtīkṛtya*) with the *avaguṇṭhana* and *dhenu-mudrās*, one should perform the worship of the sword (*khaḍga-pūjā*). Then, facing west, one should recite the mantra beginning with:
*oṃ paśupāśāya vidmahe* and so forth.
Having made the formal resolve (saṃkalpa) with water and unbroken rice grains: "O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, for Your pleasure, this animal is offered by me to You today according to my desire."
O Goddess of the gods, the *aiṃ* syllable is the abode of bound souls, suitable for use at the eastern gate;
grant to me, for Tripurā, the attainment of heaven through this as well.
Ai (3), to the illustrious Mahātripurasundarī, seize the bound soul (paśu) (2), hūṃ svāhā!
Tarpaṇa: Oṃ, you are raised up together with the light; indeed, you are auspiciousness to me, for you are truly auspicious.
This body is the work of Śiva; may you attain the state of Śiva.
Phaṭ to the weapon-mantra, the severer of the head!
With the root mantra, [one performs] the shadow [offering]; with the *tejana* mantra, [one performs] the *ārati* in the center of the head.
Having performed a prostration, having gone outside.
Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the animal sacrifice.
Now, the ritual procedure for the waving of lights (ārātrika) and the application of collyrium (nīrāñjana).
Having mixed rice flour, wheat flour, the three pungents (trikaṭu), cumin, ghee, and a large amount of sugar,
one should fashion the forms of ḍamarus— either nine, five, or three. Placing them along with camphor wicks and ghee in a vessel, one should light lamps and worship them as follows.
The third sequence: Kilhrīṃ Kāmeśvarī (1), Hskhlhrīṃ Vajeśvarī (2), Sklhrīṃ Bhageśvarī (3).
In the fifth sequence: Aiṃ is the Nivṛtti-kalā (1); Hrīṃ is the Pratiṣṭhā-kalā (2); Śrīṃ is the Vidyā-kalā (3);
Hsphreṃ is the Śānti-kalā (4); Hsauṃ is the Satyātīta-kalā (5).
Navakrama: RVLŪ Vaśinī Vāgdevatāya KLHRĪṂ Kāmeśvarī (2), NVLĪṂ Modinī (3), YLŪṂ Vimalā (4), JMRĪṂ Aruṇā (5), HSLVRYŪṂ Jayinī (6), JHMRĪṂ Sarveśvarī (7), KṢMRĪṂ Kaulinī (8), HSKRLŪṂ Mahābhairavī (9).
Thus, in sequence, there are three types.
Then, the worship: Hrīṃ (3) Guhyamālinyai (2). Then, the mantra for the eye-ointment ceremony (nīrāñjana):
Aiṃ (3) Hrīṃ! O Mahādīpa, Tejovatī, Amoghajñānaprabhā, Mālinī, Tejomaī Bhagavatī, Vicce Aiṃ! Salutation! Establish [this] in the heart! Svāhā! (2)

*Knṛil hrīṃ*, we know the Goddess Tripurā; *Hskhlhrīṃ*, let us meditate upon Kāmeśvarī; *Sklhrīṃ*, may Śakti impel us. One should recite this three times. Then, having gone to the ground on one's knees and lifted [the vessel] with both hands...
Oṃ! Having unified the inner radiance and the outer radiance into the three human beings.
Having whirled the family-lamp three times around the Goddess, one should present it.
O Goddess Navātmikā, joined with all the wheels and the lords of the wheels,
accept this lamp of the *ārātrika* for my spiritual accomplishment.
One should rotate it three times and place it upon the eastern mandala.
Having performed recitation, praise, and prostration at the primary site.
Having offered the *cadukādi* bali, and having performed the internal oblation (*antarhavana*) consisting of the worship of one's own self as the host of powers (*śaktigaṇa*), [one should proceed].

One should prepare the supreme nectar as the clarified butter (*ghṛta*), the state of bodilessness (*adehatā*) as the radiant oblation (*havis*), the mind itself as declared to be the sacrificial ladle (*śruva*), and the *suṣumnā* as the sacrificial cord (*sraj*). With the self in the form of Śiva,
having opened the mouth of Kuṇḍalinī at the base of the fire-pit (*ādhāra-grāsrakuṇḍaka*), one should offer [the oblation] according to the traditional sequence.
Thus concludes the fire offering (homa). Thus concludes the ritual procedure for the waving of lights (ārātika).
(1) Oṃ, homage to the glorious Supreme Goddess!
O Mother, O Goddess Śrī Tripurā, you are the embodiment of all times; even now, at the end of time, O Mother, you alone exist.
In the east is the goddess Unmanī, in the south is Niśeśvarī,
in the west is the goddess Kubjikā, and in the north is Guhyakālikā.
The goddess Vajravairocanī is the sovereign of the lords of the Adhāman lineage;
she is the supreme Śrī Tripurāmbikā, whose form is the upward-pointing Śrīvajra. (3)
This is the Lion-Throned Vidyā, which bestows liberation directly.
Kālikā, Caṇḍikā, Tārā, Bhairavī, and Chinnamastakā. || 4 ||
I bow to Vārāhī with her face upturned, to Durgā, the supreme Sundarī, to Bandī, Kalā, Bālā, Kubjikā, and Guhyakālikā. || 5 ||
I bow to Siddhilakṣmī, Mahālakṣmī, and the supreme Sundarī; to Jvālāmukhī, Viśālākṣī, Vimalā, and Vindhyavāsinī.
I bow to Kāmākṣā, Vatsarā, Vṛndā, and the supreme Sundarī;
I praise Kṛśānu and Savitṛ, who are illuminated by the radiance of Your splendor.
O Tripurasundarī, from you come the three times, the four aims of life,
the thirty-six principles beginning with Śiva, and the fifty letters of the alphabet.
Therefore, O Mother Tripurasundarī, [all this world arises] from you.
In the Vedāntas, there is the Great Saying (mahāvākya), which is the definitive exposition of the Veda and Brahman.
O Tripurasundarī, the Kaula path consisting of Śiva and Śakti has been proclaimed by you; O Peaceful One, the threefold path has been described to me.
O Tripurasundarī, from you [I have received] the Kaula, Yoga, and Jñāna;
O you whose form is complete, I have worshipped the knowledge of the digits of the bliss of Brahman. 11.
Having worshipped the Traipura Yoga, one shall then attain liberation;
for likewise, through the Kaula method, it quickly accomplishes all goals.
O Mother, liberation from sin is obtained through that worship; therefore, one should cause her to enter the Kaula path.
O Mother, she who is my power (*śakti*) is everywhere and at all times. 13.
May my life-force and senses sink into the lotus feet of Your honor.
May supreme devotion to the Guru and his compassionate gaze be ever with me.
He was always devoted to the family tradition [of the Kula], even in birth after birth, O Śivā.
[Thus ends the hymn to the illustrious Mahātripurasundarī, composed by the illustrious Jagatānanda.]
(1) Homage to the illustrious Supreme Deity! Homage to the Goddess Śrī Tripurasundarī!
Victory to you, O Goddess Tripurā, who are stainless and composed of light,
abiding in the midst of the moon, sun, and fire, and whose nature is divine nectar.
O Mother, O Goddess who flows through the three paths, O Sovereign of Tripura, protect me!
Victorious is the Mother of the World, devoid of qualities and change, composed of radiant light;
she who drinks the nectar of the splendor of ten million suns, and who is the destroyer of great darkness.
